# Investigative Report: Linking the Ronin Bridge and Harmony Horizon Bridge Thefts to Lazarus Group

## Executive assessment

The available evidence supports a strong public-attribution link between the March 2022 Ronin Bridge theft and the June 2022 Harmony Horizon Bridge theft. Both incidents were publicly attributed to Lazarus Group, a North Korea-linked state hacking organization. The link is supported by three principal evidence categories:

1. **Public attribution:** The U.S. Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) identified the Ronin exploiter’s Ethereum address as belonging to Lazarus Group, while the FBI later confirmed that Lazarus Group was responsible for the Harmony Horizon Bridge theft.
2. **Comparable laundering behavior:** Elliptic identified similarities between the Harmony laundering sequence and the laundering pattern previously observed in the Ronin theft, particularly the programmatic movement of stolen Ether through Tornado Cash.
3. **Blockchain and wallet evidence:** The Ronin investigation identified stolen assets, intermediary wallets, mixer deposits, decentralized-exchange activity, and later cross-chain movements. The Harmony investigation described post-theft transfers through Tornado Cash and Railgun, followed by deposits into centralized exchanges. However, the supplied evidence does not include the actual wallet addresses or transaction hashes, so the wallet evidence can be assessed only at the level of described wallet activity and attribution—not independently verified address-by-address.

The evidence supports the conclusion that the Ronin and Harmony thefts were part of a related Lazarus Group operational pattern. It does **not**, on the supplied record, independently establish that Lazarus Group and APT38 are identical entities. The sources use “Lazarus Group” and “North Korea-linked” terminology; they do not expressly identify APT38. Any APT38 linkage should therefore be treated as an unresolved analytic hypothesis rather than a source-supported fact.

## Scope, source basis, and evidentiary limitations

This report relies only on the three substantive source records supplied:

| Source ID | Publisher and date | Subject | Evidentiary contribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Elliptic, May 9, 2023 | Harmony Horizon Bridge theft | FBI attribution, Harmony laundering, Tornado Cash, Railgun, exchange deposits |
| S2 | Chainalysis, September 8, 2022 | Ronin Bridge theft | Ronin mechanics, laundering stages, cross-chain activity, seizures |
| S3 | Elliptic, March 29, 2022, updated April 14, 2022 | Ronin Bridge theft | OFAC attribution, validator compromise, Ronin laundering chronology |

A fourth supplied Elliptic URL, titled as a Harmony resource page, contains an article index rather than substantive case evidence and is not relied upon.

The source material is largely composed of investigative reporting and blockchain-analytics assessments by Elliptic and Chainalysis. These are relevant specialist sources, but several conclusions are explicitly framed as assessments, estimates, or investigative findings rather than judicially adjudicated facts. The report therefore distinguishes among **reported facts**, **attributions**, **analytic assessments**, and **uncertainties**.

## Incident summaries

### Ronin Bridge theft

The Ronin Network announced on March 29, 2022, that 173,600 ETH and 25.5 million USDC had been stolen from its cross-chain bridge six days earlier. Elliptic valued the assets at approximately $540 million at the time of theft and described the incident as the second-largest crypto theft at that point. The value was reported as exceeding $615 million when the incident was discovered because of changes in asset prices. ([S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))

According to the Ronin postmortem summarized by Elliptic, the bridge relied on nine validator nodes and required five approvals to authorize withdrawals. The attacker obtained the private cryptographic keys of five validators, thereby acquiring enough authority to approve the fraudulent withdrawals. Ronin reportedly assessed that the evidence pointed to a socially engineered attack rather than a technical vulnerability in the bridge itself. ([S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))

Chainalysis similarly described the theft as involving control of five of nine validator keys. It reported two withdrawals: 173,600 ETH and 25.5 million USDC. Chainalysis estimated that the laundering process had involved more than 12,000 addresses by September 2022. ([S2](https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/axie-infinity-ronin-bridge-dprk-hack-seizure/))

On April 14, 2022, OFAC sanctioned the Ethereum address associated with the Ronin exploiter and identified its owner as Lazarus Group. This is the strongest formal attribution in the supplied materials because it is presented as a government sanctions designation rather than solely as a private-sector analytic conclusion. ([S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))

### Harmony Horizon Bridge theft

Harmony’s Horizon Bridge was exploited on June 24, 2022, for approximately $99.7 million. The supplied Elliptic account describes the bridge as a cross-chain service for the Harmony blockchain and notes prior concerns that its centralized structure made it vulnerable to social-engineering attacks. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft))

On May 9, 2023, Elliptic reported that the FBI had confirmed Lazarus Group’s responsibility for the Harmony theft. Elliptic stated that this confirmation supported its earlier attribution, which had been based on similarities between the laundering behavior in the Harmony case and laundering patterns previously associated with Lazarus Group, including the Ronin case. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft))

The supplied material does not provide the specific Harmony exploiter address, transaction hashes, or a complete wallet graph. It does, however, describe a sequence in which stolen funds were moved through Tornado Cash, later remained dormant in several addresses, and then entered Railgun in January 2023. Elliptic further reported that funds were subsequently deposited into three cryptoasset exchanges, with Binance and Huobi publicly stating that they had identified, blocked, and seized part of the funds. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft))

## Attribution linkage between the two thefts

### Formal and public attribution

The attribution chain is sequential and mutually reinforcing:

- **Ronin:** OFAC identified the exploiter’s Ethereum address as Lazarus Group. ([S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))
- **Harmony:** The FBI confirmed Lazarus Group’s responsibility for the Horizon Bridge theft. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft))

Accordingly, both incidents have public attribution to the same North Korea-linked organization. The evidence is stronger than a simple similarity-based private-sector attribution because each incident is connected to a government attribution or confirmation. The record nevertheless does not disclose the underlying intelligence used by OFAC or the FBI, so the report cannot independently evaluate those agencies’ classified or non-public evidentiary bases.

### Laundering-pattern linkage

The most explicit investigative link comes from Elliptic’s comparison of the two laundering operations. In the Harmony article, Elliptic stated that the hackers structured transactions through Tornado Cash and that the laundering methods mirrored those used by Lazarus Group to conceal funds from the Ronin Bridge theft. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft))

The Ronin materials describe a recurring laundering sequence:

1. Stolen Ether moved to intermediary wallets.
2. Ether mixed in batches through Tornado Cash.
3. Ether swapped for Bitcoin.
4. Bitcoin mixed in batches.
5. Bitcoin deposited to crypto-to-fiat services for cash-out. ([S2](https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/axie-infinity-ronin-bridge-dprk-hack-seizure/))

Elliptic’s earlier Ronin reporting describes a related sequence: stolen USDC was swapped for ETH through decentralized exchanges; some ETH was sent through centralized exchanges; after those exchanges announced cooperation with investigators, the attacker shifted toward Tornado Cash. As of April 14, 2022, Elliptic reported that approximately $80.3 million in ETH had passed through Tornado Cash and that another $9.7 million remained in intermediary wallets prepared for laundering. ([S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))

The Harmony case followed the same broad logic: convert or route stolen assets through privacy-enhancing infrastructure, fragment the transfers, use intermediary wallets, and later attempt to reach exchanges. The pattern is not unique to Lazarus Group in the abstract; mixers, DEXs, bridges, and intermediary wallets are used by many cryptocurrency criminals. Its significance here arises from the combination of repeated behavior, temporal proximity, public attribution, and Elliptic’s direct comparison of the two cases.

### Evolution after sanctions

The sources indicate that the laundering tactics changed after Tornado Cash was sanctioned by OFAC in August 2022. Chainalysis reported that Lazarus Group moved away from Tornado Cash and increasingly used DeFi services to “chain hop,” switching among blockchains and assets. One described example involved bridging ETH from Ethereum to the BNB Chain, swapping it for USDD, and bridging the resulting asset to the BitTorrent Chain. ([S2](https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/axie-infinity-ronin-bridge-dprk-hack-seizure/))

Elliptic reported a comparable post-sanctions development in the Harmony case. In January 2023, funds associated with the theft were structured into deposits into Railgun, a privacy-oriented DeFi protocol. Elliptic estimated that approximately 70% of the Ether sent through Railgun at that time consisted of Harmony-related funds. This estimate was presented as an Elliptic research assessment, not as an independently verified official figure. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft))

The common analytical point is that the actors adapted their laundering infrastructure when a preferred mixer became subject to sanctions and heightened scrutiny. Ronin-related funds were observed in cross-chain activity after sanctions, while Harmony-related funds were described as entering Railgun. Both cases therefore illustrate a shift from a single prominent mixer toward more complex DeFi-based obfuscation.

## Wallet and asset evidence

The supplied evidence supports wallet-level conclusions at a descriptive level but does not provide enough data for independent address attribution.

| Evidence category | Ronin | Harmony | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Initial stolen assets | 173,600 ETH and 25.5 million USDC | Approximately $99.7 million in cryptoassets | Directly reported by the investigative sources |
| Initial wallet/control evidence | Five of nine validator keys allegedly compromised | Specific exploiter wallet not supplied | Stronger wallet-control detail for Ronin |
| Intermediary wallets | Reported; $9.7 million identified as prepared for laundering as of April 14, 2022 | Several post-mixer withdrawal addresses described | Supports common fragmentation behavior |
| Tornado Cash | Approximately $80.3 million reported through by April 14, 2022; later Chainalysis described broader use | Approximately $96 million attributed by Elliptic to Harmony funds | Figures reflect different dates and methodologies |
| Post-sanctions DeFi | Chain-hopping across Ethereum, BNB Chain, and BitTorrent Chain | Railgun deposits beginning January 2023 | Indicates adaptive laundering |
| Exchange exposure | More than $30 million seized with industry and law-enforcement cooperation | Deposits into three exchanges; Binance and Huobi reportedly blocked and seized some funds | Demonstrates cash-out points and intervention |

The evidence is sufficient to establish a laundering architecture involving intermediary wallets, asset conversion, privacy services, and exchange exposure. It is insufficient to identify particular wallet addresses in this report because none are included in the supplied content. Therefore, it would be improper to claim that a specific address was reused across Ronin and Harmony, or that a particular wallet was controlled by the same operator, without additional transaction-level evidence.

## APT38 question

The requested target refers to “Lazarus Group/APT38,” but the supplied sources do not name APT38. They identify Lazarus Group as a North Korea-backed or North Korea-linked hacking group and describe government attribution to Lazarus Group. No source supplied here states that APT38 is an alias, subordinate unit, operational cluster, or equivalent designation for Lazarus Group.

The defensible conclusion is therefore:

> The Ronin and Harmony thefts are publicly linked to Lazarus Group and North Korea. The supplied evidence does not independently establish an APT38 attribution.

That limitation is important because cyber-threat-intelligence naming conventions vary among governments, vendors, and researchers. APT38 may be used by some organizations as a distinct or overlapping designation, but introducing that identity here would exceed the supplied evidence.

## Contradictions and reconciliations

Several numerical differences appear in the sources, but they generally reflect different valuation dates or investigative snapshots rather than direct contradictions.

1. **Ronin valuation:** Elliptic reports approximately $540 million at the time of theft and more than $615 million at discovery. The difference is explained by cryptocurrency price changes. ([S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))
2. **Ronin total:** Chainalysis describes the theft as more than $600 million, while Elliptic uses $540 million at the theft date. These are compatible valuation descriptions. ([S2](https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/axie-infinity-ronin-bridge-dprk-hack-seizure/); [S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))
3. **Tornado Cash totals:** Elliptic reports $80.3 million through Tornado Cash as of April 14, 2022, while its later Harmony article attributes more than $468 million of Ronin funds to Tornado Cash. These figures concern different reporting periods and likely different scopes of traced activity. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft); [S3](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/540-million-stolen-from-the-ronin-defi-bridge))
4. **Harmony amount:** The theft is described as approximately $99.7 million and also as a $100 million theft. This is ordinary rounding. ([S1](https://www.elliptic.co/insights/fbi-confirms-north-korea-s-lazarus-group-as-hackers-behind-100-million-harmony-horizon-bridge-theft))

## Final findings

The most supportable overall opinion is that the Ronin Bridge and Harmony Horizon Bridge thefts were separate but closely related operations attributed to the same North Korea-linked actor, Lazarus Group. The relationship is established by public government attribution and reinforced by repeated laundering behaviors: intermediary-wallet structuring, conversion of assets, use of Tornado Cash, later migration toward cross-chain DeFi and privacy protocols, and attempted movement into centralized exchanges.

The evidence is strongest for **organizational linkage** and **shared operational tradecraft**. It is weaker for direct **wallet reuse**, because the supplied sources do not provide the addresses or transaction hashes needed to demonstrate that the same wallet controlled or received funds in both cases. Finally, the evidence does not support a conclusive APT38 identification. APT38 should remain an unverified label in this case unless additional source material explicitly maps it to the Lazarus activity described here.

## References

[https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/axie-infinity-ronin-bridge-dprk-hack-seizure/](https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/axie-infinity-ronin-bridge-dprk-hack-seizure/)
